content:
The speaker explains that:

- Algorithm running time grows with input size (e.g., sorting more elements takes longer), so we describe time as a function of input size.  
- We usually care about *upper bounds* on running time (how long it can take at most), because that gives a useful guarantee to users.  
- Knowing a program will take *no more than* a certain time (e.g., 3 seconds) is practical, especially in real-time settings, whereas knowing it takes *at least* some time gives little useful assurance.
